title: Phase 1 — promises
blurb: A proposer asks the acceptors to promise a ballot, and each acceptor answers. Which of these two steps does Paxos allow?

payload.describe: Acceptor 1 promises ballot 1, and reports its last vote.

justification.text: Paxos allows this step — there must be a request to respond to; the ballot must be higher than anything already promised. A promise is not a bare acknowledgement. It carries the ballot and value of the last vote the acceptor cast, or says it has never voted. It also raises the acceptor's promised ballot. Both halves matter: the report is how an already-agreed value is discovered, and the raise is what makes the promise binding.

payload.describe: Acceptor 1 promises ballot 1, and reports its last vote.

justification.text: Paxos does not allow this step as shown: promising must raise Acceptor 1's promised ballot to 1, and this step leaves it at 0 — so Acceptor 1 has not actually committed to anything and could still go on to accept an older ballot, which is the one thing a promise is supposed to rule out. A promise is not a bare acknowledgement. It carries the ballot and value of the last vote the acceptor cast, or says it has never voted. It also raises the acceptor's promised ballot. Both halves matter: the report is how an already-agreed value is discovered, and the raise is what makes the promise binding.

Both halves matter: the report is how an already-agreed value is discovered, and the raise is what makes the promise binding.

payload.describe: The proposer running ballot 1 asks every acceptor to promise ballot 1.

justification.text: Paxos allows this step. When a proposer asks for promises, it says which ballot and nothing else.

justification.text: Paxos does not allow this step: nobody has asked the acceptors to promise ballot 1. An acceptor only promises a ballot that some proposer actually asked it about. It does not promise ballots nobody has raised.

payload.describe: Acceptor 2 promises ballot 1, and reports its last vote.

justification.text: Paxos does not allow this step: Acceptor 2 is already committed to ballot 1, which was raised when it accepted Alice in that ballot — accepting a ballot commits an acceptor to it just as promising does. A promise has to be for a ballot strictly higher than that, and ballot 1 is the same, not higher. An acceptor promises a ballot only if that ballot is strictly higher than the highest one it has already promised. Having promised, it never goes back and promises something lower — that is what makes a promise worth anything.
